content.title: About
content.content: The multigrain bagel with raisins is a whole‑grain, ring‑shaped bread product made from a blend of wheat, rye, oats and bran, with sweet raisins folded into the dough. It has a firm, slightly chewy crust and a soft, aromatic crumb with a hint of raisin sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bagels originated in Eastern European Jewish cuisine and are traditionally boiled before baking.
The multigrain version contains at least five different grains, boosting fiber and micronutrient content.
Raisins not only add sweetness but also provide natural iron and potassium.
The classic ring shape ensures even heat distribution during baking.
Bagels are commonly served with cream cheese, smoked salmon, or hummus.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: The blend of whole grains supplies ample fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Grains provide slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Raisins contribute iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grains and raisins are good sources of thiamine, niacin and folate, which aid metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Bagels contain very little saturated fat, making them suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The bagel contains wheat and rye, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins increase the sugar level, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Despite the whole‑grain base, bagels are relatively calorie‑dense; moderation is recommended.

items.title: Phytic acid presence
items.content: Grains contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or sprouting grains can mitigate this.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bagel as a snack, split it open and spread cream cheese, avocado, hummus or smoked salmon. It also works well as a base for sandwiches, toast toppings, and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bagel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, keep it refrigerated (up to a week) or freeze, then toast before serving.
